We incorporate a minimal dark sector into a three-generation Seesaw Model, extending the standard model to include a dark sector with a $Z_2$ symmetry, known as dark parity symmetry. This extension allows us to investigate the stability of the vacuum and the dark parity symmetry itself within the context of a dark parity invariant Seesaw Model. By analyzing the generic form of the dark parity invariant neutrino mass operators, we identify the most minimal dark sector fields required to induce the smallest possible neutrino mass eigenvalues while meeting dark parity symmetry constraints. Furthermore, we examine the implications of this extension on the neutrino mass eigenvalues and the dark sector itself, finding that the minimal dark sector can be a singlet Dirac fermion pair, denoted as $S$ and $\bar S$. We also explore the phenomenological aspects of this model, including the dark parity invariant neutrino mass matrices and the minimal dark sector parameter space, in addition to predicting novel signatures for dark matter annihilation and direct detection.

Researchers who study transition metal oxides often find it necessary to balance the competing forces of spin-orbit interaction, electron-electron interaction, and crystal field splitting to achieve the desired properties. Precise control over these interactions is crucial, yet it can be challenging due to the complex and sensitive dependence of spin-orbit interaction on the position of the d orbit within the crystal field. A theoretical study has now modeled this interplay in specific materials, focusing on the well-known compounds Sr_{1-x}Ca_xTiO_{3+\delta} and Ca_{1.85}Cu_{1.85}Ti_{1.85}O_{7+\delta}. By calculating the effective spin-orbit coupling and comparing it to experimental data from X-ray absorption spectroscopy, the study reveals that electron-electron interaction can either enhance or diminish the spin-orbit coupling, and that its effects may have been misinterpreted in previous research. The findings indicate that the spin-orbit coupling in these materials is driven primarily by electron-electron interaction rather than crystal field splitting. Furthermore, the study identifies the key factors that control the spin-orbit coupling and provides a framework for understanding its behavior in a broader range of transition metal oxides.

We define a new relative $I$-function for toric complete intersections with smooth divisors, enabling us to establish a key relation between distinct relative $I$-functions. Moreover, for hypersurfaces, this relative $I$-function coincides with the previously introduced version. Notably, we demonstrate the existence of a specific relative $I$-function for toric complete intersections whose relative $I$-function corresponds to each irreducible component of the divisor. Additionally, for hypersurfaces, this yields an insightful decomposition.

Our investigation focuses on the medical imaging generation task using generative adversarial networks, specifically exploring the concept of disentangled representations. Our goal is to examine the possibility of separating and independently altering distinct components in a generated image, such as the tumor and surrounding organs, without affecting other image features. We propose an innovative approach that manipulates latent codes to achieve this control over generated images, yielding promising results in tumor segmentation. To further evaluate our method, we conduct comparative studies with current disentangled representation techniques. Our research is demonstrated using synthetic images and real-world MRI brain images, with promising outcomes.

The primary objective of the ViDaExpert system lies in facilitating the visualization of multidimensional data for users who are not data experts. To achieve this, it leverages a combination of rule-based knowledge and machine learning techniques to provide an intuitive graphical interface that enables users to effectively explore high-dimensional data spaces. From a methodological standpoint, ViDaExpert can be viewed as a pioneering example of a data visualization system that employs artificial intelligence. To fully understand the underlying functionality of ViDaExpert, this paper delves into the technical aspects of its system architecture, data preprocessing processes, and the specifics of its visualization features. To validate the efficacy of ViDaExpert, a system evaluation is conducted via a user study among 120 participants from diverse academic backgrounds. The results of this study are presented and examined from various perspectives, including the effectiveness of ViDaExpert in accurately identifying data clusters and the overall satisfaction of users with the system. To ensure the validity of findings, this paper also discusses the limitations of the current ViDaExpert implementation and suggests potential areas for future improvement.
